title: Tomb — keyed encounters
---

## T1. The Singing Door {#t1}

> The door at the end of the passage is a single slab of dull grey metal.
> It is neither warm nor cold to the touch. Lines of small runes are etched
> across it from edge to edge.
>
> An old man mutters somewhere close by. The runes catch fire one by one in
> a crackle of green light, and a haze the colour of moss rises off the metal.
>
> "Visitors again," says the old man's voice, from the runes. "The last ones
> did not leave." A dry laugh rolls out of the door.
>
> "Well. Sit, and answer me, and I will let you in."
>
> Then the door itself begins to sing, in a cracked and wandering tune:
>
> *Two brothers raised a single wall,*\
> *And each one swore it would not fall.*\
> *One took the north, and one the south,*\
> *With mortar's dust in either mouth.*
>
> *A storm came down, the wall split wide,*\
> *Each blamed the one on the other side.*\
> *Then, back to back against the rain,*\
> *They held it up and built again.*
>
> "Tell me," says the voice, "what held the wall up?"

The answer is *each other* (or the brothers working together). Three wrong
answers and the voice falls silent for a day. The right answer opens the door.
